title: Judgment Is the Decisive Skill: why leverage makes judgment the key skill
summary: Naval argues that once you have leverage (capital, people, code, media), your judgment determines outcomes. Judgment is built from experience, fast iteration and low emotion, and it earns trust through a public track record. Broad study, including philosophy, beats narrow domain reading.

principles.text: Get leverage first, then slow down and apply judgment, because leverage multiplies the cost and payoff of your decisions.
principles.quote: the first part of your career’s spent hustling to get leverage. Once you have the leverage, then you wanna slow down a bit, because your judgment really matters.

principles.text: In an age of infinite leverage, judgment is the most important skill.
principles.quote: In an age of infinite leverage, judgment becomes the most important skill.

principles.text: Leverage can be permissioned (people, capital) or permissionless (code, media like writing, podcasts, video).
principles.quote: Or you can get leverage permissionlessly by learning how to code or becoming good communicator and podcasting, broadcasting, creating videos, writing, etc.

principles.text: Build demonstrated judgment: a public track record, accountability and integrity attract leverage from others.
principles.quote: Judgment, especially demonstrated judgment, with high accountability, clear track record, is critical.

principles.text: Judgment needs experience and many fast tries, not just intellect; count attempts rather than hours.
principles.quote: If you are smart and you iterate fast, it’s not even you put 10,000 hours into something, but you take 10,000 tries at something.

principles.text: Emotions cloud judgment; the best investors and entrepreneurs see clearly and are often among the least emotional.
principles.quote: the people with the best judgment are actually among the least emotional.
